title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Fort Wayne, IN: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Fort Wayne steel mill, truck plant, aerospace electronics and INDOT bridge welding: Part C choice, Part B travel, eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Fort Wayne: Six Days for Northeast Indiana Steel, Automotive, Aerospace Electronics and Bridge Welding Inspectors
html:
Fort Wayne is a steel town in the modern sense. Steel Dynamics, one of North America's largest domestic steel producers and metal recyclers, reports from the city; its flat-rolled mill is in Butler and its structural and rail mill in Columbia City, and joist, deck and scrap operations fill out the chain. Add a pickup truck plant with more than 4,100 workers, a cluster of aerospace and defense electronics makers and a steady program of interstate bridge work, and northeast Indiana has a great many welds that need a qualified person to accept them.

The six-day Atlantis NDT course prepares Fort Wayne-area candidates for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination, whether they are maintenance welders at a mill, quality staff at a supplier, fabricators, NDT technicians or engineers. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to AWS personally and has to meet the AWS rules on education, experience and vision. Atlantis is not approved or endorsed by AWS and has no access to examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Fort Wayne. Study the six days online at your own pace with an instructor answering questions, have your employer host them at its plant for a group, or book one-to-one sessions online or in person at a location agreed when you book. Each day of the outline is described on the CWI exam prep page.

The steel chain: mills, joists and scrap

Steel Dynamics describes itself as an industrial metals solutions company, and its quarterly results carry a Fort Wayne dateline. Its Butler division, on County Road 59 in Butler, Indiana, has made hot-rolled steel coil since 1996. The Structural and Rail Division in Columbia City rolls wide-flange beams, manufactured housing beams, H-pile, angles, channels, rebar and rail for North American railroads in lengths up to 320 feet. New Millennium, the company's joist and deck business, was founded in Butler in 1999 and now runs seven plants in North America, and OmniSource, the metals recycling subsidiary, joined the company in 2007.

Inside a mill, welding is mostly maintenance and capital work: rebuilding and repairing equipment, structural repairs to buildings and crane runways, new platforms and process piping. A CWI on that work reviews repair procedures, verifies preheat on heavy sections, checks fit-up and finished welds and records what was done, often against a tight outage window. Joist and deck plants are production operations with very high weld counts, where an inspector's sampling plan and gauge discipline matter more than the verdict on any single weld. For a CWI candidate the region is unusual in offering both ends of the chain: the mills that make the shapes and coil, and the fabricators who turn steel into joists, deck and structures.

Where CWIs work in northeast Indiana

RoleTypical employerWhat the CWI checks
Fabrication QC inspectorStructural and miscellaneous steel fabricators supplying building and bridge workFit-up, welder qualifications, visual acceptance to D1.1 or D1.5, coordination of NDT
Supplier quality technician or engineerAutomotive, truck and equipment suppliersWeld size, profile and location against the drawing and the customer standard; audits of weld cells
Maintenance and projects inspectorSteel mills and large plantsRepair procedures, preheat, structural repairs, new platforms and piping
Testing agency inspectorThird-party inspection firms serving owners and contractorsBuilding steel inspection, welder qualification testing, bridge quality assurance
Welder test examinerColleges, testing labs and fabricatorsWitnessing and documenting welder qualification tests to the governing code

Light-duty pickups at Fort Wayne Assembly

GM's Fort Wayne Assembly plant opened in 1986, employs more than 4,100 people and builds mainly light-duty Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra pickups; in April 2026 it built its 11 millionth vehicle. Joining in a modern truck body shop is largely robotic and largely resistance welding, so welding inspectors in this part of the economy tend to work at the suppliers of frames, hitches, brackets and chassis components, at tooling and fixture builders, and in the maintenance teams that keep plant equipment and structures in repair.

Arc-welded automotive parts are often accepted to the customer's own weld standard or to AWS D8.8M, the automotive arc welding quality specification, neither of which is a Part C option, so a supplier inspector usually takes D1.1 for the examination and learns the customer standard on the job.

Engine controls, radios and satellite sensors

Fort Wayne has a cluster of aerospace and defense electronics. BAE Systems employs about 1,500 people across two sites in the city, a South site with 335,000 square feet of manufacturing space and a North engineering hub; its businesses there make full authority digital engine controls for commercial and military aircraft engines and airborne tactical radios. L3Harris designs and builds weather sensors for NOAA satellites in Fort Wayne, including the Advanced Baseline Imager, the Cross-track Infrared Sounder and the GeoXO Imager, supports Space Development Agency missile defense satellites, and completed an expansion of the site in April 2025.

These are electronics plants rather than weld shops, but housings, frames, test fixtures and precision metal parts bought from local suppliers can carry aerospace welding requirements. AWS D17.1, the specification for fusion welding for aerospace applications, is a Part C option in its 2024 edition. Choose it only if your drawings and purchase orders actually invoke it; otherwise D1.1 is likely to serve a Fort Wayne career better.

INDOT bridge work around the city

The transportation improvement program kept by the Northeastern Indiana Regional Coordinating Council lists the INDOT bridge projects planned in the Fort Wayne area. It includes superstructure replacements for the Minnich Road bridges over I-469, with a letting date of November 5, 2026; a superstructure replacement for the eastbound I-469 bridge over the Norfolk Southern railroad later in the decade; replacement of the Hursh Road bridge over I-69; a new bridge over US 30 at Leesburg and Felger roads; and deck overlays on I-69 and I-469, including the Spy Run Creek bridges. Deck overlays are mostly concrete work, while superstructure replacements and new bridges bring bearings, joints and, where the design calls for them, steel girders.

Where new bridge members are steel, they are normally fabricated and inspected to AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, and fabricators supplying them need inspectors who know its qualification, inspection and fracture-critical requirements. A Fort Wayne candidate aiming at bridge or highway steel should weigh D1.5 for Part C. Background: AWS D1.5.

Choosing a Part C code in northeast Indiana

  • AWS D1.1:2020. Mill maintenance and structural repairs, joist and deck plants, general fabrication and automotive supplier work. If you are unsure, this is the usual starting point.
  • AWS D1.5:2020, including Clause 12. Steel bridge members for INDOT and county work, and fabricators who supply them.
  • ASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3. Plant utilities, boilers and process piping, including the piping in mills and process plants.
  • AWS D17.1:2024. Aerospace suppliers whose drawings invoke it.
  • API 1104, 22nd edition. Pipeline and gas distribution contractors.

Each option on the AWS list carries a specific edition, which may be older than the newest one in print, so study the edition AWS names. Related reading: AWS D1.1, ASME Section IX and WPS, PQR and WPQ explained.

Ivy Tech Fort Wayne and the Johnny Appleseed Section

Ivy Tech Community College offers its Welding Technology technical certificate, 34 credit hours over three semesters, and its Structural Welding certificate, 21 credit hours over two semesters, at Fort Wayne among its Indiana locations. It also lists one-semester AWS workforce certification courses in pipe welding, shielded metal arc, gas metal arc and gas tungsten arc welding at 19 locations. Graduates heading for the CWI should note that AWS gives credit for completed trade or vocational courses, which brings the experience requirement to four years, but the work itself still has to be verifiable.

The AWS Johnny Appleseed Section is active around Fort Wayne. It held an election night at Anthis Career Center in Fort Wayne and a tour of the SDI Butler plant in 2024, a Women in Welding Night at Weld Done in Ossian in October 2025, and its annual election meeting on October 1, 2026. Section events are where to meet the inspectors, supervisors and instructors who can tell you which code books local employers favor and who may later be able to verify your experience.

Part B from Fort Wayne

AWS gives Part B only at its educational seminar locations, while Parts A and C are computer-based tests at Prometric centers. The November 2026 AWS list of CWI training locations had nothing in northeast Indiana but did include Indianapolis, Chicago, Detroit and Cleveland. The Hobart Institute of Welding Technology in Troy, Ohio, lists more than a dozen 2026 CWI sessions with AWS exam site codes; check with AWS whether a session is open to candidates outside that course. AWS's US deadline for a Part B application is six weeks before the exam date.

AWS requires 72 percent on each part, so plan for the possibility of retaking one. Once AWS accepts your application, your confirmation letter carries the eligibility code you need to book Parts A and C. The CWI exam budget calculator helps you put travel and time off into the plan. Your AWS confirmation materials also set the order of the parts and the window between the practical and the computer-based tests, so read them before booking flights or a hotel.

Experience records for mill, plant and supplier workers

A maintenance welder at a mill may have worked for several contractors and for the mill itself; a supplier quality technician may have checked welds for years without holding a torch. AWS can accept either kind of work as welding-related if it is verifiable, and AWS alone decides. List each employer and period, the processes and materials, the procedures or standards the work followed and any inspection-type duties, and add a supervisor or quality manager who can confirm it. With a high school diploma AWS requires five years; with an associate degree in welding, engineering technology, engineering or a physical science, two.

Mill outages produce good evidence if you keep it: the repair procedures you worked to, preheat logs you filled in, and the inspection or NDT reports that accepted your welds. Ask for copies or at least record the job numbers and dates while the work is fresh. One more hypothetical case: an NDT technician at a Fort Wayne fabricator, certified by the employer in UT and MT under its written practice, who has spent three years testing welds and two years before that as a fitter. Testing and inspecting welded products can be welding-related experience in AWS's eyes, and the fitting years may count too, but the technician should describe both precisely and let AWS rule on them. The vision test is separate, goes on AWS's visual acuity form, is completed by one of the professionals the form lists and must be current on exam day. The CWI requirements guide covers the full education table.

The six days at a Fort Wayne plant

For a mill, fabricator or supplier with a group of candidates, the corporate format brings the course on site. Practice can use the plant's own weld samples and gauges, from heavy repair welds to production fillets, and the code work can follow D1.1 for most groups, D1.5 for a bridge fabricator or D17.1 for an aerospace supplier whose work invokes it. The employer decides the weeks, so the course can avoid an outage or a line changeover. For a supplier, part of the practical work can set the customer's weld standard beside the code, so inspectors see where the two agree and where the customer adds requirements, and a group split between two code books can work its code exercises in both side by side.

A company can sponsor the course, but it cannot hold the credential. Each participant applies to AWS individually, provides their own experience evidence and vision record, and sits every part in their own name.

After the CWI in northeast Indiana

A new CWI might run weld inspection for a mill's capital projects, lead supplier quality for welded truck components, or inspect bridge steel for a fabricator on INDOT work. Inspectors who also want to perform NDT need method training and employer certification under a written practice; Atlantis delivers training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, for example UT Level 2 for heavy-section welds, MT Level 2 and VT Level 2, and the employer certifies the technician afterwards. AWS renews the credential at three and six years and recertifies it at nine.

Related pages: NDT training in Fort Wayne, ultrasonic testing in Fort Wayne, magnetic particle testing in Fort Wayne, NDT training in Indiana, and CWI exam prep in Indianapolis, Detroit and Chicago.

Sending a Fort Wayne enquiry

Tell us the number of candidates, the format you prefer, the Part C code book you expect to use and when you aim to sit the exam. For a plant group, give the site and the weeks that fit around production or outages. If you are unsure whether your experience meets the AWS rules, describe it briefly and we will tell you what to confirm with AWS. Quotes are given on request for the format you choose, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Fort Wayne?
faq.a: The AWS Johnny Appleseed Section holds events in and around Fort Wayne, including an election night at Anthis Career Center, a tour of the SDI Butler mill and a Women in Welding Night in Ossian. Its annual election meeting was held on October 1, 2026.

faq.q: Where would a Fort Wayne candidate take Part B?
faq.a: At an AWS seminar location. In November 2026 AWS listed Indianapolis, Chicago, Detroit and Cleveland, and the Hobart Institute in Troy, Ohio, lists 2026 sessions with AWS site codes. Parts A and C are taken at Prometric centers.

faq.q: Which code suits a maintenance welder at a steel mill?
faq.a: AWS D1.1 for most mill structural and equipment work. If much of your work is boiler or process piping, consider the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3.

faq.q: Should an inspector at an aerospace electronics supplier choose AWS D17.1?
faq.a: Only if your drawings and purchase orders invoke it. D17.1:2024 is on the AWS Part C list, but many Fort Wayne roles are better served by D1.1.

faq.q: Can I use AWS D8.8M for Part C?
faq.a: No. AWS D8.8M, the automotive arc welding quality specification, is not on the AWS list of Part C code books. Automotive supplier candidates usually choose AWS D1.1.

faq.q: I completed the Ivy Tech Welding Technology certificate. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: Completed trade or vocational courses bring the AWS experience requirement to four years of welding-related work. Whether the certificate counts as such a course, and whether your jobs count as welding-related, is for AWS to decide. Keep records of every job.

faq.q: Can a mill or plant host the six days?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format delivers the six days at the employer's facility for a group, using its welds and gauges, in weeks the employer chooses. Each participant applies to AWS individually.

faq.q: Is the course endorsed by AWS?
faq.a: No. The course carries no AWS approval or endorsement, and Atlantis never sees examination content; AWS runs the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Fort Wayne?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Fort Wayne. Candidates study online at their own pace, as a group at the employer's facility, or one-to-one online or in person somewhere agreed at booking. The Atlantis offices are in Houston and Hyderabad.

faq.q: How do I request a quote from Fort Wayne?
faq.a: Send the enquiry from this page with the format, the number of candidates and the Part C code you plan to use. We quote for that format and come back to you within one business day.
